items.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: That particular one, the Bobby Flay show, the original show, it was actually the director who came

ctx.x: Yeah. And you go from something like that to Food Channel TV series. So when you get contracted for something like this, does the producer have suggestions for you?

Yes. These days more suggestions than we probably like. That particular one, the Bobby Flay show, the original show, it was actually the director who came, his name is Wayne Page, a TV director that I’ve worked with, I’ve known him for years and done odds and ends projects for him. This was a case where he was doing “Hot Off the Grill” it was Bobby’s first show. And they just wanted a theme. So he came to me and sat and watched over my shoulder while I created it. And that was it. It was fun to do. It was…
It’s a kind of a one-shot.
